```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Make a function to calculate a two-sample t test, then apply it to data.

## Function

```{r functions}
my_mean <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sum(x) / length(x)
}

my_var <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sum((x - my_mean(x))^2) / (length(x) - 1)
}

my_t_test <- function(x, y) {
  nx <- length(x); ny <- length(y)
  vx <- my_var(x); vy <- my_var(y)

  se <- sqrt(vx / nx + vy / ny)
  t  <- (my_mean(x) - my_mean(y)) / se
  df <- (vx / nx + vy / ny)^2 /
        ((vx / nx)^2 / (nx - 1) + (vy / ny)^2 / (ny - 1))
  p  <- 2 * pt(-abs(t), df)

  list(t = t, df = df, p.value = p)
}
```

## Apply to data: mpg of automatic (am = 0) vs manual (am = 1) cars

```{r apply}
auto   <- mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 0]
manual <- mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 1]

my_t_test(auto, manual)

# Compare: t, df, and p-value should match
t.test(auto, manual)
```
